transcript:
Header: 2026-06-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes | Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Sofia (CSM), Ethan (NovaPulse Head of ML), Priya (SRE), Grace (CTO)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR, we wanted to run through usage, costs, reliability, and next quarter roadmap for NovaPulse. Sofia and Jordan are here to help with the technical bits. How's everyone doing?

[00:08] Ethan: Doing good, thanks. Busy month, we've spun up more embedding jobs for the nightly search refresh which bumped token counts.

[00:15] Jordan: Yeah I pulled the usage, I can share the dashboard after this — looks like embeddings went up ~3.4x month-over-month for late May into June, generation is relatively flat but sessions have longer contexts. That explains the token cost uptick.

[00:28] Priya: Quick clarity question — when you say embeddings, is that per record, or the batch reindex? Because our reindex pipeline changed to do per-chunk embeddings which multiplies calls.

[00:36] Ethan: It's the per-chunk change, we wanted fresher vectors. Might be a candidate for batching or prefix caching you mentioned earlier.

[00:44] Liam: Right — so a few things to note: hosted API pricing hits you per token, embeddings are charged per vector unit; with Dedicated you get predictable throughput and lower per-unit cost but you trade off burst elasticity. There's also Redwood Optimize suggestions like batching the embedding calls and longer KV cache retention for search queries which could cut costs substantially.

[01:05] Grace: Can you ballpark savings? Our CFO wants to know if Dedicated is worth a reserved commit vs staying hosted.

[01:10] Liam: Off the cuff — if you sustain the current peak throughput, Dedicated could lower per-token cost by 25–40% depending on utilization and quant profiles. But we want to give you a model: Jordan will run a benchmark against your sample workload to show realistic numbers.

[01:22] Jordan: I'll need your sample prompts and a representative traffic trace — p95 tokens, concurrency numbers. Priya, can you share that?

[01:27] Priya: Yes, I'll export the trace. It's around p95 3.2k tokens and concurrent workers 18 during peak.

[01:34] Jordan: Perfect, that helps. For latency SLOs, Dedicated has predictable latency when properly sized; we do kernel selection and batching heuristics that help. There was a note in your ticket about a 5xx spike last week — can you summarize?

[01:46] Ethan: We saw about a 20-minute window with 5xx errors — roughly 0.6% of requests, mostly around a deployment window in eu-west. We routed traffic to the us-east fallback but the client noticed increased error rate.

[01:58] Sofia: We looked at the logs; it lined up with a capacity brief overflow on the hosted cluster for that region. Our incident was short, but I get why you flagged it. We pushed a region fallback rule that should make that seamless next time.

[02:12] Grace: Is there something we should change on our end to avoid hitting that?

[02:16] Jordan: Two levers: you can configure automatic fallback to a secondary region (we already enabled that for your account) and we can set a soft reject threshold to maintain p99 latency under load. Also, pre-warming Dedicated nodes avoids cold-queue pressure.

[02:35] Ethan: Sounds good. What about private deployment? Our security team is eager but wants timeline and what is required for VPC/transit.

[02:43] Sofia: For Private we've got two paths: customer-managed VPC where we deploy into your cloud account, or an on-prem package. The shortest path is customer VPC — typically 6–10 weeks for SSO, KMS integration, and audit work, longer if you require on-prem. I will send the checklist.

[02:58] Priya: We need to see the KMS flow — are you supporting our HSM-backed keys?

[03:02] Liam: We support KMS integrations and in many enterprise cases couple with HSM. I'll include the security doc link (https://redwood.example.com/security.pdf) — Sofia will also send a one-pager.

[03:12] Ethan: You mentioned quantization and performance. What's the tradeoff on output quality for our use case?

[03:18] Jordan: Good question — for most retrieval+generation flows, 8-bit or 4-bit quantized variants give ~1–3% quality delta on our evals while saving 30–60% on cost. We'll run your eval set (we saw your eval harness from onboarding) to show measured deltas. If generation fidelity for certain prompts is critical, we can pin those routes to higher-precision variants and route other workloads to quantized model variants.

[03:44] Grace: Nice, route-by-policy is important for us. Can policies be per-route in the API?

[03:49] Jordan: Yes, per-route model pinning and fallbacks are supported. You can also do A/B rollouts and automatic fallback to a higher-precision model if output quality drops.

[04:00] Priya: Back to costs — will batching suggestions be automated or manual?

[04:05] Sofia: Currently Optimize gives suggested batching configs; we can also enable auto-batching heuristics in your runtime. We'll show expected savings after Jordan's bench.

[04:13] Ethan: Ok, can you show the last quarter's usage trend?

[04:16] Liam: Sure, quick recap — May embeddings spike due to reindex, generation steady, session length up 12% and average tokens/session up 18%. That explains the month-over-month bill change. I'll send the charts.

[04:30] Grace: Any reliability KPIs we should track in the console?

[04:33] Sofia: Console shows token-level costs, per-route p95/p99, error rates, traces. We can set alerts for p95 > 800ms or error rate > 0.5% for a given region.

[04:44] Ethan: That's useful. Can we get a report for the last 90 days with top cost drivers?

[04:48] Liam: Yes — action item for me: cost driver report by workload.

[04:52] Priya: About the 5xx spike — do you have a permanent incident report?

[04:56] Sofia: I'll attach the postmortem to the ticket and share the link after the call; it includes root cause and the mitigation we've applied.

[05:05] Grace: On roadmap — any upcoming features that matter for us?

[05:09] Jordan: A few items: improved KV cache retention controls (Q3), finer-grained auto-batching, and a new quantization profile UI in Optimize. Also improving warm-up/scale gates for Dedicated to reduce cold-start latency.

[05:24] Ethan: Timeline for KV retention?

[05:26] Jordan: Early Q3 for beta, GA late Q3. Sofia will add you to the beta list.

[05:31] Grace: Good. Questions from my side — legal will want to see SOC 2 and data residency assurances.

[05:37] Sofia: We'll send the SOC 2 summary and list of regions supported for private deployments. For data residency in a VPC deployment, data stays in your VPC under the deployment model.

[05:47] Priya: For the benchmarking, do you need us to pause traffic or can you replay traces?

[05:52] Jordan: We can do both. Replaying traces against a Dedicated cluster gives a more faithful measure, but we might also do a shadowing run. We'll coordinate with Priya.

[05:59] Ethan: Let's pick replay first then a short live window.

[06:04] Liam: Great — to recap actions: Liam will send cost model and charts, Jordan will schedule/execute the benchmark, Sofia will share security docs and roadmap beta invites, Priya will share traces and confirm stakeholders. We'll reconvene after the benchmark to decide on Dedicated pilot.

[06:21] Grace: That works for me, thanks everyone.

[06:25] Liam: Thanks, we'll follow up with notes and links.

[06:29] (Call ends)

Notes and links referenced during call:
- Security one-pager: https://redwood.example.com/security.pdf
- Benchmarks dashboard (internal): https://redwood.internal/bench/novapulse (will share access)
- Postmortem ticket for eu-west incident: TICKET-9843
- Optimize docs / batching guide: https://docs.redwood.com/optimize/batching

Transcription notes: occasional mis-heard product names ("Redwood Dedicate" -> "Redwood Dedicated"), slight timing offsets for overlapping talk, some punctuation omitted as in raw transcript.
